## Description

<!--
Provide an explanation of your issue in an arbitrary form. Provide any additional information, suggested solution and as much context and examples as possible.
If work on your issue requires account credentials please provide them or explain how one can obtain them.
-->

I've been trying to download all the videos(member and non-member using ```--cookies```) from a channel's community page, but I keep getting the incomplete data received error. The problem is that it's stuck on page 1 and I guess the API JSON download fails, preventing subsequent pages from being found. I've tried using youtube-dl but it gives the same result, though without the "Downloading API JSON" message. If there are any videos on page 1 then yt-dlp will download it, but it won't proceed to the next page to download more. I can download the videos from later pages if I manually get the video URL. 

I tried just a basic command ```--list-formats``` on something like https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCl_gCybOJRIgOXw6Qb4qJzQ/community
and only the videos on the first page would be displayed(if there are any).

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

`--download-sections` leads to strange download section selection. I've noticed that when I was downloading from pornhub, but I'm not sure if it's a pornhub-related bug. Sometimes it works properly and downloads just requested sections, but quite often downloads a random portion of video.

I'm using the following Dockerfile configuration (only a relevant part here):

    FROM debian:buster
    
    RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        git python3 python3-pip python3-setuptools build-essential ffmpeg apache2 php curl ca-certificates \
        python3-certifi python3-brotli python3-websockets python3-mutagen python3-pyxattr python3-secretstorage \
        php-sqlite3 sqlite3 \
     && apt-get clean \
     && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
    
    RUN pip3 install yt-dlp
    
    VOLUME /var/www/html/youtube-dl/downloads
    
    ENV LANG=en_US.UTF-8
    ENV LC_ALL=C.UTF-8

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

- [X] Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
- [ ] If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead

items.title: [Hotstar] MPD manifest requests consistently fail with HTTP 475 (Forbidden), resulting in "No video formats found" for playable episodes

labels.name: cant-reproduce
labels.description: The issue cannot be reliably reproduced

labels.name: account-needed
labels.description: Account details are needed to test/fix this

items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I've read the [**NO AI / NO LLM POLICY**](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#no-ai--no-llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated

- [x] I've checked that all URLs and arguments with special characters are [properly quoted or escaped](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ#video-url-contains-an-ampersand--and-im-getting-some-strange-output-1-2839-or-v-is-not-recognized-as-an-internal-or-external-command)
- [x] I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
- [x] I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required

### Region

India

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

The **JioHotstar** extractor successfully retrieves video metadata, server time, and browser cookies, but every attempt to fetch the DASH (MPD) manifest fails with `HTTP 475: Forbidden`. Since the extractor cannot obtain any streaming manifests, yt-dlp reports "No video formats found" despite the content metadata being available, indicating a likely change in Hotstar's playback authorization or manifest access mechanism that is not currently handled by the extractor.

#### Environment
- **yt-dlp version:** `stable@2026.07.04`, `nightly@2026.07.20.234742`, `master@2026.07.20.234245`
- OS: Windows 11
- Browser cookies: Firefox (683 cookies extracted successfully)
- FFmpeg: 7.1
- Target site: Hotstar
- VPN Connection: Yes (NordVPN - India)

#### **Extraction Flow**

The extractor successfully performs the initial steps:

✅ URL recognized by [JioHotstar](https://hotstar.com) extractor
✅ Metadata JSON downloaded
✅ Server time retrieved
✅ Authentication cookies loaded
✅ Episode metadata parsed correctly

#### **Observations**
 
- Authentication appears to be working since metadata endpoints are accessible.
- Browser cookies are being correctly imported.
- Custom `User-Agent` and `Referer` are supplied.
- The extractor never receives a playable MPD manifest.
- The failure occurs before format extraction, leaving the formats list empty.

#### **Likely Root Cause**

The log suggests that JioHotstar has introduced new playback authorization requirements for DASH manifest requests, such as:

- additional playback tokens,
- updated DRM/session validation,
- stricter CDN authorization,
- new signed manifest URLs,
- or extra request headers required by the playback API.

Because metadata retrieval succeeds while manifest retrieval fails with HTTP 475, the issue appears isolated to the playback/manifest acquisition stage rather than general authentication.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

- [x] Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
- [x] If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
- [x] Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I'm reporting that yt-dlp is broken on a **supported** site
- [x] I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
- [x] I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
- [x] I've checked that all URLs and arguments with special characters are [properly quoted or escaped](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ#video-url-contains-an-ampersand--and-im-getting-some-strange-output-1-2839-or-v-is-not-recognized-as-an-internal-or-external-command)
- [x] I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
- [x] I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required

### Region

Kazakhstan

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

When downloading Twitcasting.tv livestream output file ends up with stuttering audio and video. 

This error persists on any livestream. Tested:
1) with/without cookies
2) with/without password
3) when connecting via VPN
4) when connecting via different ISP
5) on different devices
6) with FFmpeg versions 7.1.1/6.0

When downloading VOD stream warning "Found duplicated MOOV Atom. Skipped it" is absent and output file is fine.

Example below stopped manually (CTRL+C), but error also persists when stream downloaded from the start with "--wait-for-video" argument.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

- [x] Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
- [ ] If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
- [x] Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

latvia

I record live stream from tiktok which requires login. I use cookie from browser. When i start recording in CMD is written:
F:\yt-dlp>yt-dlp --cookies=cookies.txt https://www.tiktok.com/@username/live

then came:

after it yt-dlp deleted file which was recorded and started to write video into new file.
I.e. on every disconnect yt-dlp deletes file.
I use newest nightly 2025.12.15.233113 version.

labels.description: This will not be worked on

items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I'm requesting a feature unrelated to a specific site
- [x] I've looked through the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#readme)
- [x] I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
- [x] I've searched the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar requests **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

First, since I'm not using Python as my development language, I can't utilize the progress hook and have to rely on progress-template instead.

During video downloads, I noticed that video and audio progress are reported as two separate stages. However, what I really need is the overall download progress combining both video and audio. After assuming "audio file size is consistently 2% of video size," I achieved satisfactory results through additional calculations.

The problem emerged when I added subtitle downloads. I observed that subtitles constitute another separate download stage, typically appearing first—before video downloads. Since not every video has subtitles, sometimes the first stage shows subtitle download progress, while other times it directly shows video file download progress.

This makes it impossible to determine whether the current download stage is for subtitles or video, rendering my overall progress calculations highly inaccurate.

After extensive research, I found no existing solution. The closest approach would involve the `max_progress` and `progress_idx` parameters (if I understand them correctly), but these seem to be available only in the progress hook, not in progress-template.

My suggestion is to expose `max_progress`, `progress_idx`, and ideally a stage type identifier in progress-template. Without this, if yt-dlp ever changes subtitle downloads to occur in a third stage, my overall progress calculations would face catastrophic errors again.

Best regards.

items.title: Coalesce adjacent fragments from the same file in the fragment downloader
items.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I'm reporting a feature request
- [X] I've looked through the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#readme)
- [X] I've verified that I'm running yt-dlp version **2022.04.08** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update)) or later (specify commit)
- [X] I've searched the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=) for similar issues including closed ones. DO NOT post duplicates
- [X] I've read the [guidelines for opening an issue](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#opening-an-issue)

### Description

Sometimes, when media are served with a fragment manifest, all the defined fragments are actually adjacent byte ranges from a single file (example: <https://arte-cmafhls.akamaized.net/am/cmaf/100000/100200/100225-000-A/220414121352/100225-000-A.m3u8>).  Currently, yt-dlp downloads all each of those ranges separately; for each byte range the socket has to be opened, the encryption negotiated, the HTTP headers sent, etc. This creates some pretty large overheads due to HTTP and TLS framing, and lowers download speed due to repeatedly going through the TCP slow start phase. But since the ranges are adjacent, it should be possible to download them all together, in bulk. This would save on bandwidth and make the download speed more stable.

At some point we should probably also think about taking advantage of HTTP keep-alive and pipelining, but that would be a separate issue. Coalescing adjacent ranges from the same file seems comparatively easier than that.

~~Please apply 2b22577760833ff17d2a113d041fda41eb1426cf before testing.~~

items.title: [YouTube] 403 for a short period of time(a few seconds), then the link can be downloaded normally

labels.name: cant-reproduce
labels.description: The issue cannot be reliably reproduced

items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I'm reporting that yt-dlp is broken on a **supported** site
- [x] I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
- [x] I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
- [x] I've checked that all URLs and arguments with special characters are [properly quoted or escaped](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ#video-url-contains-an-ampersand--and-im-getting-some-strange-output-1-2839-or-v-is-not-recognized-as-an-internal-or-external-command)
- [x] I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
- [x] I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required

### Region

US

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

I'm not sure what has changed recently on YouTube. After getting the download link, there will be a 403 status for a few seconds, and then it can be downloaded normally. I have verified that this problem exists in all clients that require js player, but not android_vr, and they all appear in itag 18 format. This has nothing to do with po token, because I have tried using po token as well and it still doesn't work

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

- [x] Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)

items.title: Fail to resume download after Http error 416
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I'm reporting a bug unrelated to a specific site
- [x] I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
- [x] I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

If a 416 response is received when attempting to download a file via `HttpFD`, a second attempt is made to determine the current length of the file:
```py
            except HTTPError as err:
                if err.status == 416:
                    # Unable to resume (requested range not satisfiable)
                    try:
                        # Open the connection again without the range header
                        ctx.data = self.ydl.urlopen(
                            Request(url, request_data, headers))
```
However, if the `headers` object already contains a `Range` value, it will be included in the second request as well. As a result, another 416 error will be returned and the download will fail.

Since `headers` is an instance of `HTTPHeaderDict`, in the following code
```py
            request = Request(url, request_data, headers)
            has_range = range_start is not None
            if has_range:
                request.headers['Range'] = f'bytes={int(range_start)}-{int_or_none(range_end) or ""}'
```
the `Range` header is added not only to the `request` object but also modifies the original `headers` object. This happens because when the `request` is created, it stores the original `headers` object instead of creating a copy:
```py
    @headers.setter
    def headers(self, new_headers: Mapping):
        """Replaces headers of the request. If not a HTTPHeaderDict, it will be converted to one."""
        if isinstance(new_headers, HTTPHeaderDict):
            self._headers = new_headers
        elif isinstance(new_headers, Mapping):
            self._headers = HTTPHeaderDict(new_headers)
        else:
            raise TypeError('headers must be a mapping')
```

But even if the setter performed copying, that still wouldn't guarantee the absence of `Range` in `headers`, because this value could have been passed via `info_dict['http_headers']`.

So I suggest, before making the second request, explicitly calling `headers.pop('Range', None)`.

items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I'm reporting that yt-dlp is broken on a **supported** site
- [x] I've verified that I'm running yt-dlp version **2026.03.17** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update)) and confirmed I'm on the latest version (`yt-dlp is up to date`)
- [x] I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
- [x] I've checked that all URLs and arguments with special characters are properly quoted or escaped
- [x] I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue) and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues) for similar issues **including closed ones** — no existing report found

### Region

United States

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

Any Audius track fails to extract with:

```
ERROR: 'list' object has no attribute 'startswith'
```

**Root cause:** The Audius discovery-node API now returns a `"mirrors"` key inside the track's `artwork` object, whose value is a **list** of mirror hosts (not a string URL):

```json
"artwork": {
  "150x150":   "https://.../150x150.jpg",
  "480x480":   "https://.../480x480.jpg",
  "1000x1000": "https://.../1000x1000.jpg",
  "mirrors": [
    "https://creatornode2.audius.co",
    "https://audius-creator-17.theblueprint.xyz",
    "https://audius-content-10.figment.io"
  ]
}
```

`AudiusBaseIE._real_extract` (`yt_dlp/extractor/audius.py`, ~L142-152) iterates **every** key/value pair in `artwork` and assigns the value directly to a thumbnail's `url`, assuming all values are strings:

```python
artworks_data = track_data.get('artwork')
thumbnails = []
if isinstance(artworks_data, dict):
    for quality_key, thumbnail_url in artworks_data.items():
        thumbnail = {
            'url': thumbnail_url,   # <-- becomes a list when quality_key == "mirrors"
        }
        ...
```

So one thumbnail ends up with `'url': [<list>]`, which then crashes in `YoutubeDL._sanitize_thumbnails` → `sanitize_url()` → `url.startswith('//')`.

**Suggested fix** — skip non-string values (consistent with the file's existing `isinstance` guards):

```diff
             for quality_key, thumbnail_url in artworks_data.items():
+                if not isinstance(thumbnail_url, str):
+                    continue  # e.g. artwork["mirrors"] is a list of hosts, not a URL
                 thumbnail = {
                     'url': thumbnail_url,
                 }
```

With this one-line guard applied locally, extraction and download succeed normally.

- [x] If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
